name: Trastuzumab emtansine

discovery.note: Trastuzumab linked through the non-cleavable thioether linker SMCC to the maytansinoid DM1, about 3.5 drug molecules per antibody.

tagline: First ADC for a solid tumour: trastuzumab carrying the microtubule poison DM1
summary: Trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) is an antibody–drug conjugate that delivers the cytotoxic maytansinoid DM1 to HER2-overexpressing cancer cells. It is used in previously treated metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer and as adjuvant therapy for residual disease after neoadjuvant treatment.
mechanism: The trastuzumab component binds HER2 and retains its signalling-inhibitory and ADCC activity. After binding, the conjugate is internalised and degraded in lysosomes, releasing lysine-SMCC-DM1.

DM1 binds tubulin and inhibits microtubule assembly, causing mitotic arrest and cell death. Because the linker is non-cleavable, the released payload is charged and poorly membrane-permeable, limiting bystander killing.
uses: HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer after trastuzumab and a taxane
Adjuvant treatment of HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant therapy

history.title: Collaboration
history.detail: Genentech licenses ImmunoGen's maytansinoid conjugate technology for use with trastuzumab.

history.title: EMILIA trial
history.detail: T-DM1 improves progression-free and overall survival versus lapatinib–capecitabine.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved as Kadcyla in February, the first ADC approved for a solid tumour.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Approved in the European Union in November.

history.title: KATHERINE and adjuvant approval
history.detail: T-DM1 halves the risk of recurrence versus trastuzumab in residual disease; FDA approves the indication in May.

history.title: Displaced in second line
history.detail: DESTINY-Breast03 shows trastuzumab deruxtecan superior to T-DM1 in metastatic disease.

pk.metabolism: Catabolism of the antibody; released DM1 metabolised by CYP3A4/5

serious: Hepatotoxicity including liver failure and nodular regenerative hyperplasia
safety.boxed_warning: Hepatotoxicity, cardiac toxicity and embryo-fetal toxicity; do not substitute for or with trastuzumab.

facts: The US name 'ado-trastuzumab emtansine' was chosen partly to reduce confusion with trastuzumab.
It was the first antibody–drug conjugate approved for a solid tumour.
